title: Phenylpropanoid Amides from Buteae monospermae Semen as Hepcidin-Modulating Candidates for Anemia of Inflammation: Network Pharmacology, Deep Learning Prediction, and In Vitro Validation
summary: Deep-learning affinity prediction helped prioritize two Butea monosperma compounds for follow-up. In IL-6-stimulated HepG2 cells, both dose-dependently reduced hepcidin; this is an in vitro candidate result, not evidence of treatment efficacy.
ai_technology: Deep-learning affinity prediction with network pharmacology and in vitro assays

evidence.tested: Deep-learning affinity prediction helped prioritize two Butea monosperma compounds for follow-up. In IL-6-stimulated HepG2 cells, both dose-dependently reduced hepcidin; this is an in vitro candidate result, not evidence of treatment efficacy.
evidence.unknown: The study evaluates the reported models and datasets only; broader generalization and real-world deployment outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning affinity prediction ranked candidate targets for Butea compounds, alongside network pharmacology, docking and molecular dynamics; the cell assay tested the prioritized candidates.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
